request.input: Filming location: Apartment set — Film City Stage 3. City: Mumbai, IN. Location type: kind: stage. Research the rules and practical constraints that apply to a film production shooting here: which authority issues the filming permit, the typical lead time and fee band, any night-time noise curfew as a time range, whether camera drones and pyrotechnics are allowed, other filming restrictions, the nearest emergency hospital, and any monsoon flooding history. Prefer official municipal, police and civil-aviation sources. Leave a field empty rather than guessing.

permit_authority.description: The authority that issues filming permits for this location, by name.

permit_lead_time_days.description: Typical lead time to obtain a filming permit, in days. Empty if unknown.

fee_band_inr.description: Typical permit or location fee range in INR. Empty if unknown.

noise_curfew.description: Local night-time noise restriction as a plain time range, e.g. '22:00-06:00'. Empty string if there is no curfew.

drone_rules.description: Rules on flying camera drones here — say plainly whether drones are prohibited, permitted with permission, or unrestricted.

fireworks_rules.description: Rules on pyrotechnics or fireworks here — say plainly whether they are prohibited or permitted with a licence.

restrictions.description: Other filming restrictions that apply at this location, one per item.

nearest_hospital.description: Nearest hospital with an emergency department, and approximate distance.

monsoon_flooding_history.description: Known monsoon waterlogging or flooding history for this area.

content.permit_lead_time_days: 2 days (48 hours) when no temporary structure is erected; up to 15 days when temporary/semi-permanent structures are involved
content.monsoon_flooding_history: Film City Road and the main approach to Film City have experienced monsoon waterlogging/flooding (reported instance in August 2025) causing submerged roads and traffic jams
content.drone_rules: Permitted with permission — DGCA regulates drone operations nationally; camera-drone use at Film City will require DGCA clearance plus any local approvals/NOCs
content.fireworks_rules: Permitted only with licence/compliance — a Fire Compliance Certificate under the Maharashtra Fire and Life Safety Act (and other fire-safety approvals) is required before pyrotechnics are used
content.noise_curfew: No specific municipal night-time noise-curfew time range is stated in the Film Shooting policy documents consulted (no explicit curfew time found)
content.permit_authority: Assistant Commissioner (Ward), Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) — designated nodal authority for film shooting permissions in the ward
content.nearest_hospital: Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital (major emergency hospital serving Goregaon East area) — approximately 4–6 km from Film City depending on route
content.fee_band_inr: Base/commercial scrutiny fee ₹66 per sq. metre of built-up area; temporary/alternative rates cited up to ₹425 per sq. metre; revalidation lump-sum charge example ₹15,000; a 10% surcharge provision is noted
restrictions: Fire compliance certificate (Maharashtra Fire and Life Safety Act) required before pyrotechnics or fire-hazardous activities
Structural stability certificate / plans signed by an architect/licensed surveyor required for temporary/semi-permanent sets
Police NOC (local police and traffic police) and NOC from property/owner are required for filming on municipal roads/public areas

lines permissions are proposed to be granted by MCGM. As per GR provisions, permissions at government locations would be granted through State Single Window. 2\. The MCGM already grants temporary film shooting permission on MCGM, Municipal premises such as open ground, roads, schools, garden, cemeteries, market etc (vide no. अ. अ/ ओडी/ ९७०/ आ.ज . दि. 16.10.2015) but not on private premises. Therefore, such shooting permission with temporary, semi-temporary structures are allowed. 3\. It is mandatory for premises owner to obtain permanent trade licence under section 394 of MMC Act 1888, where continuous shooting activity is being carried out. Licensed indoor locations need not have to take permission for every shooting, if no extra temporary structure is erected.
